_comment: Seeds the journeys stage runs every time, so that what a random run once
found is checked deliberately from then on. `fixed` is the CI set: short
runs, chosen for coverage rather than for having failed. `regressions` is
where a shrunk failure goes -- seed, length, and what it caught, so the
entry says why it is here rather than just that it is.
This is the same bargain corpus.js makes: findings graduate from random to
named. A seed that only ever passes is cheap to keep and worthless to

fixed.note: general coverage. Once verified against the build before 9991e50, where it failed at action 30 with `?volunteer=` returning an event twice for an account holding two signups on it -- but see _staleNote: this seed no longer walks that sequence.
general coverage, different action mix. Also once caught that duplicate, at action 10; see _staleNote.

_staleNote: What a seed catches is only true for the action sequence it drew when the
claim was written, and the sequence moves whenever the number of draws per
action changes. `create-event` began varying its activity count -- one
`ctx.rnd()` call -- and every seed below started walking somewhere else.
So the notes above record what these seeds *found*, which is why they were
kept, and no longer describe what they do today. That is worth knowing
before trusting one: a seed promoted for catching a specific defect stops
guarding that defect the moment the stream shifts, and nothing announces
it. A regression that must stay caught belongs in a written test, not in a
